assaka:
1assaka
m. [assa3 + ka2; S. aśvaka], a small horse; a toy horse; Sp 204,.23 (°-rathakādīhi bālakīḷanakehi kīḷamāno) = Ps III 291,.22; — assako in Ee at Ja VI 515,14´ is prob. wr; Be assavirahito; Ce, Se anassako yeva.

2assaka
mfn. [S. asvaka], without property, poor; owning nothing; M I 450,.34 (puriso daḷiddo ~o anāḷhiyo); II 68,.25 (~o loko sabbaṃ pahāya gamanīyan ti; Ps III 306,.20 : ~o ti nissako sakabhaṇḍarahito) ≠ Paṭis I 126,.32; A III 352,.1 (daliddo ~o anāḷhiyo iṇaṃ ādiyati).
dakkha:
1dakkha
mfn. [S. dakṣa], able, adroit, dexterous; clever, skilled; Abh 721; Vin III 135,.9 (kumārikā abhirūpā … paṇḍitā vyattā medhāvinī ~ā analasā; Sp 552,.27 : ~ā ti chekā); D I 74,.1 (~o nahāpako vā nahāpakantevāsī vā); M I 125,.8 (dāsī … ~ā analasā susaṃvihitakammantā); A II 27,.27 (yo hi tattha ~o analaso sampajāno patissato ayaṃ vuccati bhikkhave bhikkhu porāṇe aggaññe ariyavaṃse ṭhito); Th 740 (so atthavā so dhammaṭṭho so ~o so vicakkhaṇo); Ja VI 246,1* (~aṃ ca posaṃ manujā viditvā; 246,11´ : ~an ti dhanuppādanakusalaṃ); Sp 900,.14 (~ā ti chekā avirajjhitvā sīghaṃ kattabbakāriṇī ti attho); 993,.27 (kiccesu °-tā); Dhp-a I 419,.20 (bahūsu pana pupphesu santesu cheko mālākāro ~o kusalo bahū mālāguṇe karoti); Ap-a 235,.14 (opammakusalo upamā-upameyyesu ~o); Sadd 331,.31 (dakkhati kusalakamme aññasmiṃ ca kiccākicce adandhatāya sīghaṃ gacchatī ti ~o cheko yo kusalo pi vuccati); — ifc see rūpa-.

2dakkha
n. [S. dākṣya], dexterity, ability, skill; Ja III 466,13* (~aṃ gahapataṃ sādhu, Se so; Ce, Ee dukkhaṃ; Be ~aṃ gahapatī; 466,15´ foll. : gharāvāsaṃ vasantānaṃ gahapatīnaṃ bhoguppādanatthāya anālasyachekakusala-bhāvasaṅkhātaṃ ~aṃ nāma sādhu dakkhabhāvo bhaddako, Be so; Ce, Se dukkhaṃ … dakkhabhāvo laddhako; Ee dukkhaṃ nāma sādhu dakkhabhāvo laṭṭhako); — see also dakkhiya, dakkheyya.

3dakkha
m. [from dakkhati4; cf S. darśa, dṛkṣa], appearance; sight; — ifc see duddakkha.

Vv 81:16 (mudūhi pāṇīhi ~ehi ca, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee jāla-; Vv-a 315,.30 foll. : jālavantehi abhilohitanakhehi, tena jālahatthataṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ tambanakhataṃ anuvyañjanaṃ ca dasseti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee jālihatthataṃ).

2jāli(n)
mfn. [from jāla2], possessing flames; S I 69,22* (pahūtabhakkhaṃ ~inaṃ pāvakaṃ kaṇhavattaniṃ daharo ti nāvajāneyya).

2ka
[ts] (nom. ko2), 1. a suffix added to nouns, pronouns or adjectives, usually not affecting the meaning, but sometimes forming adjectives or diminutives or expressing contempt; cf Sadd 661,.30 (sabbanāmato kakārāgamo); 803,.17 (hīḷanānukampa-khuddakakucchitasakatthesu ko); very often added to bahuvrīhi cpds; cf Sadd 774,.30 foll.; — 2. a suffix added to numerals to express a group; cf Sadd 801,.5 (anekatthe dvādito ko, satassa dvikaṃ dvisataṃ); —       °-kāra2,    m. [ka + kāra1], the suffix -ka; Sadd 661,.30 (sabbanāmato ~’-āgamo yathātanti); Thī-a 28,.2 (sumuttikā ti sumuttā, ~o padapūraṇamattaṃ); Paṭis-a 413,.31 (~o pan’ ettha anukampāya daṭṭhabbo); Sv-pṭ III 47,.6 (muṇḍake samaṇake ti ettha ~o garahāyan ti).

3ka

(frequently followed by particles, esp. by nu, nu kho, (s)su, ssa); who are you who …?; sometimes expressing indignation: who does he think he is to …? who are you to …?; Vin I 7,.12 (kassa nu kho ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, ko imaṃ dhammaṃ khippam eva ājānissati); 28,.35 (kimhi nu kho ahaṃ ālambitvā uttareyyan ti … idha bhante bhagavā ālambitvā uttaratū ti); 104,.4 (kissa antarāyiko, paṭhamassa jhānassa adhigamāya antarāyiko); II 10,.38 (kvāyaṃ abalabalo viya); 286,.24 (kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ); III 132,.27 (kassāhaṃ kena hāyāmi; Sp 551,.13 : ahaṃ kassā aññissā itthiyā kena bhogena vā alaṅkārena vā rūpena vā parihāyāmi, kā nāma mayā uttaritarā ti dīpeti; Sadd 217,.24 : ettha kassā ti pañcamiyā rūpaṃ); 135,.11 (ete kho bhante amhe na jānanti ke vā ime kassa vā ti); IV 212,.29 (kyāhaṃ taṃ ayye na icchissāmi; Sp 901,.3 : kyāhan ti kiṃ ahaṃ); 274,.14 (kā imā ti, bhikkhuniyo ayyā ti); D I 18,.9 (taṃ kissa hetu); 96,.8 (ko n’ eva re m’ ayaṃ dāsīputto samāno Khuddarūpiṃ dhītaraṃ yācatī ti); 237,.8 (kismiṃ vivādo); II 31,.5 (kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti); M I 132,.12 (kassa kho nāma tvaṃ moghapurisa mayā evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi; Ps II 104,.5 : tvaṃ moghapurisa kassa khattiyassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā … mayā evaṃ dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāsi; perhaps rather for ko ssa?); II 159,.3 (imassa kv attho); III 6,.1 (ettha kyāhaṃ bho Gotama karomi, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee kvāhaṃ, prob. wr); 238,.18 (kaṃ si tvaṃ bhikkhu uddissa pabbajito ko vā te satthā kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesi); S I 39,3* foll. [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll. [upa + hadati (or ud + hadati); cf S. upahadana and BSU §110], defecates (upon); soils (with excrement); Vin I 78,.12 (senāsanaṃ ~anti pi ummihanti pi, Ce, Se so; Be uhadanti; Ee wr ūhananti); III 227,.27 (santhatāni … yesaṃ no dārakā ~anti pi ummihanti pi, Ce, Se so; Be uhadanti; Ee wr ūhananti; Sp 685,.2 foll. : santhatānaṃ upari vaccaṃ pi passāvaṃ pi karontī ti) quoted Sadd 382,.13; Vin IV 40,.2 (yattha kākā vā kulalā vā na ~anti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr ūhananti); Ja II 355,10´ (~āma pi omuttema pi); Dhp-a II 181,.10 (indakhīlaṃ dārakādayo omuttenti pi ~anti pi, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ~ayanti, prob. wr); — fut. 1 sg. *ūhacchaṃ, Ja II 71,16* (idāni kho taṃ ūhacchaṃ, esā amhāka dhammatā, so read with BSU §110? Be ohacchaṃ; Ce, Ee ūhacca; Se ohaccaṃ; 71,19´ : vaccan te sīse katvā pakkamissāmi); —     pp (a) ūhata,   mfn., soiled (with excrement); Vin II 222,.22 (sace vaccakuṭī ~ā hoti, dhovitabbā; Sp 1286,.21 : ~ā ti ūhaditā, bahi vaccamakkhitā ti attho, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se ~ā ti ohanitā); — ifc see kāka-; —  (b) ūhadita,   mfn., soiled; Sp 1286,.21 (ūhatā ti ~ā, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se ohanitā); —  (c) * ūhanna,   mfn. [cf S. lex. hanna], soiled (with excrement); defecated on; Ja II 73,13* (aggihuttañ ca ~aṃ tena bhinnā kamaṇḍalū, so read with BSU § 110? Be uhannaṃ; Ce ūhantaṃ; Ee ūhanti; Se ūhanaṃ); — see also ohadati.

ṭhāyi:
ṭhāyi(n)
-ṭṭhāyi(n) mfn. [S. sthāyin], being or living in; staying, remaining; lasting for; resting on; Pv 11:9 (icc eva maccā paridevayanti adāyakā pecca yamassa ~ino; Pv-a 59,.27 foll. : yamalokasaññite yamassa ṭhāne pettivisaye ṭhānasīlā); — ifc see āruppa-, oja- (sv ojā), kappa-, pariyuṭṭha-; — see also isīkaṭṭhāyiṭṭhita (sv isīkā), esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhita (sv esikā).
